generation_review.prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid:
U+3D072. LEFT component: ONE vertical stem joins THREE horizontal bars; bottom longest, middle shortest and top intermediate. RIGHT UPPER component: EXACTLY FIVE approximately parallel upright strokes, evenly spaced left to right. Each extends ABOVE and BELOW TWO shared horizontal crossbars, which are gently curved/arched as in THX; the two crossbars join all FIVE uprights, producing exactly FOUR enclosed white narrow vertical fields IN ONE ROW (not two rows, not five fields). Preserve all five upper tips and all five lower tips. No third crossbar in lattice. BELOW this lattice, separated by a clear gap in coherent THX/QJZ/DYC form, a wide horizontal bar spans about the lattice width or slightly more. From the UNDER SIDE of that bar descend exactly TWO separate long gently outward-curving legs. No central third leg and no stem joining lattice to lower bar. Preserve the left three-bar stem as separate from all right parts. Smooth constant-width strokes, round caps, no brush swells.

visual_review.method: white inspection composite compared against all available reference specimens
reading_criteria: Left three-bar stem: bottom slightly longer than top; middle shortest.
Right lattice has exactly five uprights, two crossbars and four counters in one row, with five tips above and below.
Lower wide bar is detached from lattice and carries exactly two descending legs; no third middle leg.
notes: All four specimen overviews and enlarged views compared. Native preserves five uprights/four fields and detached lower two-leg form in coherent THX/QJZ/DYC-type construction.
Lattice and lower bar remain separated; lower bar spans approximately lattice width.
caveats: Gap between lattice lower tips and lower bar is modest; tracking and heavier weights must preserve it.
CCZ uses a touching central-stem variant; native intentionally retains detached attested form.

visual_reference_review.reviewer: independent visual structural review by stroke_font_engine
notes: All four references compared. Accepted THX-like bowed lattice whole construction: exactly five uprights crossed by two curved horizontal levels, producing four adjacent counters in one row.
Lower right horizontal is detached from every lattice lower tip, with two descending curved legs attached below. Left component retains its three horizontal levels and single vertical.
Left upper and bottom bars are nearly equal, bottom slightly longer; middle is shorter. Lattice gaps and the modest but clear separation above the lower detached bar remain essential.
limitations: Visual comparison against the supplied chart raster; not specialist paleographic certification.
Does not verify historical writing order, exact metrics, or final font stroke width.
Verdict applies only to the source PNG hash recorded here.
